key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can passivate the back contact of 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells without extra Cu, Na, or Ag, enabling over 16% efficiency and a record VOC of 552 mV.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for high-voltage chalcopyrite bottom cells, supporting tandem-solar-cell integration with a low-bandgap absorber.
method: Formed GaOx by ion exchange during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber.
Tested whether added Cu, Na, and sputtering oxygen flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Analyzed the structural state of the GaOx layer and optimized the passivating hole transport layer in finished devices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an optimized CuInSe2 bottom solar cell with active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
watch_item: The conductive behavior appears sensitive to how the GaOx layer forms, so process reproducibility and interface control are likely critical for scale-up.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
